subject: physics_2
question_text: Describe a transistor and explain its working.

verification.note: The 1+2+2+2+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two figures carry 0 marks because the question does not ask for a diagram. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the book prints 'a small base correct' for base current, 'reverse bised', 'penitrate', and 'As the base in lightly doped'; all are written correctly here. The current-gain definitions α = I_C/I_E, β = I_C/I_B and β = α/(1 − α) are ADDED — the book gives only I_E = I_B + I_C. Physics hand-checked: the emitter is heavily doped, the base thin and lightly doped, the collector moderately doped; the emitter-base junction is forward biased and the collector-base junction reverse biased in both types; in p-n-p the carriers crossing the base are holes and in n-p-n they are electrons; conservation of charge at the device gives I_E = I_B + I_C, and dividing through gives β = α/(1 − α). Symbols with capital-letter subscripts are authored as KaTeX, which Unicode cannot encode honestly. FIGURE NOTE: the battery plate lengths are drawn to the correct polarity for each type — in p-n-p the emitter side of the left battery is positive and the collector side of the right battery is negative; in n-p-n both are reversed. The current arrows follow the conventional current: into the emitter for p-n-p and out of the emitter for n-p-n. Both figures were rendered and inspected before this card was filed.

recall_prompt: Describe the transistor — its three sections and their doping — then explain the p-n-p and n-p-n working and give the current relation.

steps.label: Transistor
lines: A transistor is a device which consists of
two p-n junctions. It is also called a
junction transistor.
The name comes from transfer of
resistance from the input to the output.
There are two types: p-n-p and n-p-n.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two p-n junctions, and both types named.
steps.why: Two junctions in one crystal is what separates a transistor from a diode. Naming both types at the start also sets up the two halves of the working that follow.
common_mistakes: Saying it has one p-n junction. That is a diode.
Saying it is made by joining two separate diodes. The three regions are parts of one crystal.

recall.must_convey: That a transistor is a single device with two p-n junctions, of two types, p-n-p and n-p-n.
accept: device with two p n junctions
junction transistor
two types p n p and n p n

steps.memory_tip: One junction is a diode; two junctions in one crystal is a transistor.

lines: i) Emitter (E): the section at one end. It

lines.text: is heavily doped and supplies the

lines: ii) Base (B): the section in the middle. It

lines.text: is very thin and lightly doped, so most
of the injected carriers pass through it

lines: iii) Collector (C): the section at the other

lines.text: end. It is moderately doped and

lines: In both types the emitter-base junction
is forward biased and the collector-base
junction is reverse biased.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Each section needs its doping level, and the base needs the word THIN as well.
steps.why: The doping levels are not descriptive detail — they are the design. Heavy emitter doping supplies plenty of carriers, and a thin lightly doped base means few of them recombine there, so nearly all reach the collector. That is why the collector current is almost as large as the emitter current.
common_mistakes: Saying the base is heavily doped. It is lightly doped, and thin.
Leaving out the biasing sentence. Both junctions and both biases are needed.
Saying the collector is the most heavily doped section. The emitter is.

recall.must_convey: That the emitter is heavily doped, the base thin and lightly doped, the collector moderately doped, with the emitter junction forward biased and the collector junction reverse biased.
accept: emitter heavily doped supplies the carriers
base is thin and lightly doped
collector moderately doped and collects the carriers
reject: holes cross the emitter base junction

steps.memory_tip: Heavy, thin and light, moderate — emitter, base, collector, in that order.

steps.label: p-n-p connection
steps.margin_note: Basic connection of a p-n-p transistor. The emitter side of the left battery is positive; the collector side of the right battery is negative.
steps.why: The battery polarities are the whole figure: the long plate is the positive terminal, and here the positive terminal faces the p-type emitter. That is what forward biases the emitter junction and pushes holes towards the base.
common_mistakes: Reversing the batteries. In p-n-p the emitter side is positive.
Forward biasing the collector junction as well. It must be reverse biased.

recall.must_convey: That the p-n-p figure shows p, n, p regions with the emitter junction forward biased and the collector junction reverse biased.
accept: p n p with two batteries
emitter junction forward biased, collector junction reverse biased
draw the basic connection of a p n p transistor

steps.memory_tip: Positive plate faces the p-type emitter. p for positive.

steps.mark_note: Hole flow through all three regions

lines.text: and the base is n-type. The emitter-base
junction is forward biased and the

lines: ii) Holes in the emitter are repelled by

lines.text: base. This is the emitter current.

lines: iii) The base is thin and lightly doped, so

lines.text: only a few holes recombine with
electrons there. This small flow is the

lines: v) Inside the transistor the current is

steps.margin_note: Two marks. Follow one hole from the emitter, through the base, to the collector — and name each current as it appears.
steps.why: The three currents are three stages of the same flow of holes, not three separate things. Because the base is thin and lightly doped, only a small part of that flow is lost there, so the collector current is nearly the whole emitter current — which is what makes the device useful as an amplifier.
common_mistakes: Saying the base current is large. It is small, because the base is thin and lightly doped.
Saying electrons carry the current inside a p-n-p transistor. Holes do.

recall.must_convey: That holes leave the emitter, most cross the thin lightly doped base to the collector, and only a few recombine there giving the small base current.
accept: holes cross the emitter base junction into the base
few holes recombine so the base current is small
most holes reach the collector
reject: electrons cross the emitter base junction

steps.memory_tip: p-n-p carries holes. Follow one hole and the three currents name themselves.

steps.label: n-p-n connection
steps.margin_note: Basic connection of an n-p-n transistor. Both batteries are turned round: the emitter side is negative, the collector side positive.
steps.why: The n-p-n figure is the p-n-p figure with every polarity reversed, because the carriers that must be pushed out of the emitter are now electrons instead of holes. Drawing them one under the other makes that single difference obvious.
common_mistakes: Copying the p-n-p battery polarities. Both are reversed for n-p-n.
Writing p, n, p under the three regions. For n-p-n it is n, p, n.

recall.must_convey: That the n-p-n figure shows n, p, n regions with both battery polarities reversed from the p-n-p case.
accept: n p n with the batteries the other way round
emitter side negative and collector side positive
draw the basic connection of an n p n transistor

steps.memory_tip: Same picture, every polarity flipped — and n, p, n instead of p, n, p.

junction is forward biased and the

base. This is the emitter current.

holes there, giving the small base

steps.margin_note: Two marks. The same four stages as the p-n-p case, with electrons in place of holes.
steps.why: Only the carrier changes. Because electrons move faster than holes in the same material, n-p-n transistors are the ones used in most circuits — the same reason the NOT gate circuit earlier in this chapter uses an n-p-n transistor.
common_mistakes: Saying holes cross the base in an n-p-n transistor. Electrons do.
Saying the current in the external circuit is carried by holes. Outside the crystal it is always electrons.
Making the base current the large one.

recall.must_convey: That electrons leave the emitter, most cross the thin lightly doped base to the collector, and only a few recombine there giving the small base current.
accept: electrons cross the emitter base junction
few electrons recombine so the base current is small
most electrons reach the collector
reject: holes cross the emitter base junction

steps.memory_tip: Same four stages, electrons instead of holes.

steps.label: Current relation
lines: Whatever leaves the emitter arrives
either at the base or at the collector:
The current gains are defined as
α is a little less than 1 and β is large,
which is why a transistor can amplify.
steps.margin_note: Eighth mark. The relation itself is the marked line; the two gains are worth adding.
steps.why: The relation is just conservation of charge: no carrier disappears, so the emitter current splits between the base and the collector. Because the base takes only a small share, α is close to 1 and β = α/(1 − α) becomes large — a small base current controls a much larger collector current.
common_mistakes: Writing I_B = I_E + I_C. The emitter current is the largest of the three.
Writing β = α. The two are different; β = α/(1 − α).
Saying α is greater than 1. It is always a little less than 1.

recall.must_convey: That the emitter current equals the base current plus the collector current, with α = I_C/I_E and β = I_C/I_B.
accept: I E equals I B plus I C
alpha is collector by emitter current
beta is collector by base current

steps.memory_tip: The emitter current splits two ways, so it is the biggest of the three.

insider_note: The two workings are the same four stages twice — holes for p-n-p, electrons for n-p-n. Write the p-n-p case carefully and the n-p-n case is a rewrite with one word changed.
